What | learned from the training:
During the internship, | learned a lot of technical and professional knowledge, essentially
bridging the gap between the classroom theory and actual software engineering. In a
technical sense, | became more familiar with the Laravel ecosystem, spatial data, and
middleware, as well as the hard truth that success in local development does not translate
to success in the production environment, particularly when dealing with the quirks of the
server configuration, 403 errors, and other Issues. | discovered that data visualization is only
as useful as the bad or good data that it is based on, and that administrative platforms must
be balanced with powerful management tools and also strict security guardrails. From a
professional perspective, | was taught the art of clear stakeholder communication to set and
adjust expectations, to avoid feature creep, and to prevent the drain on a project when the
goals are not aligned. Showing systems to end-users to them was a lesson in the importance
of responsive iteration, thorough training, and eliminating small frictions in UX. Last but not
least, | leamned about disciplined time management, the importance of code quality in highpressure scenarios and the versatility and flexibility needed to work across multiple roles in
an IT fast-paced work environment, all thanks to a transformative Emotional Intelligence
seminar.

What I did in the training:
During my comprehensive On-the-Job Training at the Philippine National Police (PNP) Station
in Manolo Fortich | was lucky enough to take part in administrative data management,
technical IT support, and digital multimedia design. This was all meant to improve how the
station handles its daily operations, in a practical way i mean. One big part of my responsibility
was dealing with front-facing public service and database administration, where | would
systematically handle verify, and process citizen accounts through the National Police EClearance portal. | was also assigned to digital transcription, encoding important office
documents, turning physical paper records into more organized digital databases, and
reviewing internal financial information so | could compute the station's annual expenses
using Excel spreadsheets.
On the more technical side, and hardware support spectrum, | did routine maintenance and
hands-on computer troubleshooting. | had to disassemble and reassemble computer units,
just to check internal component compatibility, and then diagnose laptop audio driver issues.

Technology background, | spearheaded UI/UX design and interface improvements for the
PNP Operation Office planning system. | incorporated modern, user-centered layout
frameworks like Bento Grids so the platform feels more natural, and easier to move around
without confusion.
Aside from system development, | regularly handled creative and multimedia tasks as well.
For example, | edited, scaled, and printed official event tarpaulins. | also framed symmetrical
certificate layouts while placing watermarks with precision, and | refined PowerPoint
presentation slides so the content stays clear and well understood. Lastly, | complemented

What | did in the training:
From February 24, 2026, to May 25, 2026, | had the chance to be an intern student at the |
Guidance Counseling Office. During my internship, | learned a lot, my technical skills got
better, and | understood how much responsibility, teamwork, and professionalism really
matter in the workplace. This experience became one of the most meaningful parts of my
school journey, because it let me put in practice what we discussed in class... into real tasks,
and actual duties.
On our first day, we were given a quick briefing about our responsibilities in the office. Our
supervisor explained what we needed to do during the whole internship period. One main
task was to create an inventory system, that could store and manage the data of all NBSC
students. Since student records are not just important but also sensitive, we were told to build
a system that can protect confidential information, through an encryption-based approach. At
the start, the tasks looked difficult and kinda overwhelming, but with teamwork, patience, and
our supervisor's guidance, we slowly understood the process step by step, bit by bit.
While developing the system, we faced several issues like organizing data the right way,
making sure everything stays accurate, and keeping the security of confidential files. These
moments helped us sharpen our problem-solving skills and critical thinking. We also learned
that dealing with student information means you have to be responsible and careful, because
even a small mistake can affect records that matter. Because of that, we realized how
essential it is to be observant and careful in every assigned task, no matter how minor it
seems.
After finishing the system development, we supported our Host Training Establishment
(HTE) during the enroliment period, by using the system we created. We helped with
encoding, sorting, and handling student information more efficiently. It was satisfying to see
that the system became useful, making the enroliment process faster and more orderly. Other
than assisting during enroliment, we were also expected to maintain the system up until the
last day of our duty. We monitored its performance, fixed small concerns when needed, and
made sure the data stayed accurate, and protected.
Throughout the internship, we didn't only improve our technical knowledge. We also
developed values like discipline, cooperation, respect, and dedication to work. We learned
how to communicate in a professional manner with office staff, and how to work effectively as
a team member. This experience showed us that real-world tasks demand patience,
commitment, and steady learning, even when things get tiring.

What | did in the training:
During my On-the-Job Training (OJT) at the Public Employment Service Office (PESO) here
in Manolo Fortich, under the supervision of Sir Jerome, | learned a lot by doing two main
types of work. First, | helped build a website for a local job portal. Second, | helped with
daily office tasks, public events and face-to-face customer service. This internship helped
me improve my computer programming skills and taught me how to work well with a team in
a real office.
For the computer work, | was part of a team where my main task was to build and improve
specific parts of the job portal using Laravel. | focused on coding some of the pages for the
job seeker portal and dashboard for the OFW portal. | wrote code for user logins, secure
logouts, data privacy pop-ups and specialized navigation forms. To make sure my work met
the office requirements, | asked Ma'am Jalou to review the OFW portal that | was assigned
to develop. Her feedback helped me identify areas for improvement and ensure that the
portal met the needs of its users. Working on these team tasks was a great experience
because it allowed me to take what | learned and use it to enhance and improve my own
individual project. To save my work and share it with my team, | used GitHub, where |
learned how to fix code errors and recover deleted files when something went wrong.
Outside of computer programming, | was fully involved in helping the office run smoothly. |
spent many days encoding paper forms into the official PESO Employment Information
System. | also helped check test papers and modules, calculate total scores and record the
final grades for Job Start and SPES trainees. During big public events at the ABC Hall, |
operated the laptop and projector so the presentations could run without any technical
glitches.
During my last few weeks, | volunteered to work at the front desk to help clients get their
PESO clearances. | made sure they signed the logbook, guided them on how to fill out their
profile forms and collected their satisfaction surveys. Overall, this experience taught me how
to use technology to help the community and prepared me for a professional career.

[This training gave me a comprehensive and practical education in full-stack software |
development, system design, and real-world problem solving. From the earfiest weeks
working with Google Apps Script, | leamed how critical proper authorization, ingger
configuration, and environment variable management are when building automated

the live Foundation Day event taught me that testing in a controlled environment Is very
different from production under real user load, and that third-party platform imitations such
as AP] quotas can fail a system at the worst possible moment, making failover planning and
scalability thinking essential from the start. Building the Lost and Found Management

Planning the database schema before writing any code, choosing the right technology stack,
and structuring the API around real administrative workflows all taught me haw much upfront
thinking prevents costly rework later. Building the admin dashboard showed me that a

work in the later weeks gave me a much more mature perspective on what it means to build

caching showed me how architectural decisions accumulate into real user experience
problems over time. Overall, this training strengthened my ability to think through problems
methodically, build iteratively, and take genuine ownership of a system from its first line of
code to its final production-ready state.

experience in handling office records, managing documents, and
working in a professional environment.

What I did in the training:
During my comprehensive On-the-Job Training at the Philippine National Police (PNP) Station
in Manolo Fortich, i was given the chance to actively join in a mix of administrative data
management, technical IT support, and digital multimedia design, all aimed at making the
station's day to day workflows run smoother. A big part of my responsibility was the front
facing public service side as well as database administration, where | handled, checked, and
processed citizen accounts in an organized way through the National Police E-Clearance
portal. | was also assigned to encode important office documents, turn physical paper records
into structured digital databases, and review internal financial information to compute the
station's yearly expenses using Excel spreadsheets.
On the technical and hardware side, | conducted routine maintenance and did hands-on
computer troubleshooting. This meant disassembling and reassembling computer units so i
could inspect internal component compatibility, diagnosing laptop audio driver problems,
fixing printer paper jams, and supporting network security by troubleshooting Wi Fi
connectivity then updating system passwords. At the same time, because i have a
background in Information Technology, | spearheaded UI/UX design and interface refinement
for the PNP Operation Office planning system. | used modern, user centered layout
approaches, like Bento Grids, to make the system easier to navigate and more intuitive.
Aside from system work, | also handled creative tasks. For example, | edited, scaled, and
printed official event tarpaulins, then arranged symmetrical certificate layouts with exact
watermark placements, and improved PowerPoint slides for clearer presentation. Lastly, i
complemented all these technical duties by attending an operational orientation about quick
coordination during emergency rescue operations, and i assisted at the front desk too,
receiving station visitors, responding to public inquiries, and maintaining professionalism
throughout.
